title: Seller Performance Standing — Severity Credit in Top-Performer Relief
content:
**Credit.** The severity credit is the clean-severity credit of 1 point for a seller whose record carries no active points from intellectual property, inauthentic complaint, product authenticity or review manipulation violations, the stepped-down credit of 0.5 point for a seller whose active serious points all come from serious violations recorded six or more whole calendar months before the handling date, and nothing for a seller with a serious violation recorded in the last six whole calendar months.

The credit forms part of top-performer relief under Seller Performance Standing. It is added to the relief points before the sum is rounded down to a whole point, the top-performer cap then applying to the result.

## Records read

- **Active serious points** — the points recorded for intellectual property, inauthentic complaint, product authenticity and review manipulation violations, less every point expired, stepped down, relieved or reversed on entries carrying any of those types.
- **Serious violations in the last six whole calendar months** — those from whose recording date fewer than six whole months have passed to the handling date, counted by calendar date.

## Decision table

| Active serious points | Serious violation recorded in the last six whole calendar months | Severity credit |
|---|---|---|
| none (zero or less) | — | 1 point |
| above zero | none | 0.5 point |
| above zero | one or more | nothing |

## Worked figures (hypothetical)

- Relief points 2.4 with a credit of 0.5 make 2.9, which rounds down to 2; with a credit of 1 they make 3.4, which rounds down to 3.
- A seller's only serious violation, an intellectual property violation, was reversed when the complaint was retracted: no active serious points, credit 1 point.
- A product authenticity violation recorded eight whole months ago still carries points after its step-down, and no serious violation was recorded since: credit 0.5 point.
